nodes.rationale: The builder is framed as architect + product/UX designer + AI/Python/DB/DevOps engineer at once so that no feature is accepted purely because it was requested; the identity exists to license refusal of low-value work.
nodes.community_name: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything

nodes.label: Feature Justification Rule
nodes.rationale: Every feature must save employee time, reduce mistakes, increase revenue, improve customer experience, or produce business insights. 'Nothing else gets built' is the explicit stop-rule that keeps scope from expanding into generic software.
nodes.community_name: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything

nodes.label: Project Goal
nodes.rationale: Quality bar set by naming reference products (Apple, Notion, Linear, Stripe, Raycast) fused with a classic skeuomorphic truck-stop aesthetic, so 'premium' has a concrete target instead of being taste-by-argument.
nodes.community_name: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything

nodes.label: Manual Processes Replaced
nodes.rationale: Paper passes, reminder calls, monthly boards, walking the lot with paper, manual search, manual renewal tracking, manual payment tracking — the concrete inventory of labor the system must delete.
nodes.community_name: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything

nodes.label: Design Philosophy
nodes.rationale: 'DO NOT create a boring dashboard' — every screen is purpose-built rather than a generic table view, because a generic view would push the owner back to scanning instead of reading an answer.

nodes.label: Modern Skeuomorphism UI Style
nodes.rationale: Soft shadows, raised cards, rounded controls, glass overlays, warm truck-stop colors, micro-interactions, hover elevation, loading skeletons and beautiful empty states — physicality is used so a paper-native operator trusts the screen the way they trusted the pass.

nodes.label: Dark Mode and Light Mode
nodes.rationale: Both themes are mandatory because the same operator uses the app inside the office and outdoors in the lot at night.

nodes.label: Brand Colors
nodes.rationale: Primary #173F35 forest, Secondary #E6E0D4, Accent #D6862B amber, Success #1FAF67, Danger #D74A4A, Warning #E7B416, warm ivory background — a fixed token set so status color never becomes ad hoc per screen.

nodes.label: Typography System
nodes.rationale: Originally SF Pro for body, but SF Pro only exists on Apple devices, so on Windows/Android the stack fell through to Segoe UI or Inter and Inter headings sat next to an OS-chosen body face — the UI rendered differently on every machine. Collapsed to one family (Inter) differentiated by weight; the only deliberate contrast left is Inter vs JetBrains Mono.

nodes.label: Inter (headings and body)
nodes.rationale: One family for both headings and body, differentiated by weight, to guarantee identical rendering across Windows, Android and Apple devices.

nodes.label: JetBrains Mono (numbers)
nodes.rationale: Mono is reserved for what a truck stop reads as data — truck numbers, plates, receipt numbers, money — so the type itself signals 'this is a value you can compare character by character'.

nodes.label: Tech Stack
nodes.rationale: Next.js/TypeScript/Tailwind/Framer Motion/Shadcn front end over a FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + PostgreSQL + Redis backend, Celery for background jobs, JWT with role-based access, local storage that is cloud-ready, Docker on Linux behind Nginx.

nodes.label: Reusable Claude Skill Folder
nodes.rationale: Skills at C:\Users\nikhi\OneDrive\Desktop\begineer-claudeskills\agent-skills-main must be reused rather than reinvented, so implementation effort goes into the parking domain instead of rebuilding generic tooling.
nodes.community_name: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything

nodes.label: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything
nodes.rationale: The owner should never need to remember anything — memory is moved from the human to the system, which is the root justification for reminders, audit log, payment history and derived insights.
nodes.norm_label: core principle: the software remembers everything
nodes.community_name: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything

nodes.label: Daily Pass ($20, custom day range)
nodes.rationale: Fixed $20 price with a custom-length expiration window (7/3 to 7/4, or 7/3 to 7/6), so a multi-day stay is still sold as daily rather than forcing a weekly upsell.

nodes.label: Monthly Pass ($250 default, overridable)
nodes.rationale: Default $250 but the owner can override per company (4 trucks for $900, 12 trucks for $2500) because fleet pricing at a truck stop is negotiated, not listed.

nodes.label: Owner Price Override / Special Pricing
nodes.rationale: Negotiated per-company fleet rates must be stored on the company profile so the price survives staff turnover and is not re-negotiated from memory each month.

nodes.label: Accepted Payment Methods
nodes.rationale: Cash, check, credit, debit and phone payment (card taken over the phone) today; online payment is explicitly deferred to future.

nodes.label: Parking Objects (Vehicle Types)
nodes.rationale: Truck, trailer, car, bobtail, flatbed and personal vehicle — a trailer or a personal car can occupy a spot on its own, so the object model cannot assume every occupant is a truck.

nodes.label: Parking Pass Fields
nodes.rationale: Exactly twelve fields (truck number, trailer number, plate, company, phone, parking type, price, start date, end date, payment method, notes) and 'nothing more' — every extra question costs the driver time at the window.

nodes.label: Parking Rules (First Come First Serve, No Refunds)
nodes.rationale: No reservations and no refunds; the customer agrees before paying and that agreement is stored digitally so a later refund dispute is settled by the record rather than by argument.
nodes.norm_label: parking rules (first come first serve, no refunds)

nodes.label: Monthly Customers
nodes.rationale: A company may hold 1, 5 or 50 trucks and all of them must roll up to one company profile showing total/active/expired trucks, renewal rate, payment history, outstanding balance, last reminder, favorite spot notes and special pricing.

nodes.label: Spot Holder Logic
nodes.rationale: Monthly customers leave a personal car to hold their spot; when the truck returns the car leaves and the truck parks. Occupancy must therefore be modeled as 'reserved by vehicle' plus a spot timeline, not as a single static assignment, otherwise the lot reads as full-of-cars.

nodes.label: AI Search
nodes.rationale: Declared 'the biggest feature'. The owner standing in the lot types a truck number, trailer number or plate and within one second sees PAID / NOT PAID / Expired / Expires Today / Expires Tomorrow, monthly status, outstanding balance, company, phone, history and payment notes — one query replaces walking the lot with paper.

nodes.label: AI Parking Inspector
nodes.rationale: The in-lot presentation of a search hit: a single green card carrying PAID, expiry date, company, plan and payment method, so the owner never opens multiple pages while standing next to the truck.

nodes.label: Smart Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Explicitly 'instead of numbers, generate business intelligence' — revenue by period, occupancy, available spots, renewals, average stay, top/late/churning companies, peak days and hours, revenue and renewal forecasts.

nodes.label: AI Insights / Morning Manager Report
nodes.rationale: Generated every morning without being asked: expiring passes, likely renewals, late payments, companies worth calling, daily customers eligible for monthly, unused capacity, risk customers, repeat visitors, loyal companies.

nodes.label: Monthly Reminder System
nodes.rationale: Only monthly customers get reminders, at 7 days / 3 days / 1 day before and on expiration day, friendly and professional. Restricting the audience and the cadence is what keeps it from reading as spam.

nodes.label: Daily Customer Tracking
nodes.rationale: Track truck frequency, company frequency, visits and total spend; at roughly ten daily passes the system automatically recommends a monthly plan, converting churn-prone walk-ins into recurring revenue.

nodes.label: Weekly Customer Tracking
nodes.rationale: Explicitly 'same logic' as daily customers — same frequency/spend tracking and the same automatic monthly-plan recommendation.

nodes.label: AI Sales Opportunities (Hot/Warm/Cold Leads)
nodes.rationale: Visit count and spend (e.g. 14 visits, $280) are turned into a ranked hot/warm/cold lead list with a concrete recommendation, so upsell is a queue rather than a memory exercise.

nodes.label: Company Profiles
nodes.rationale: One page per company holding all trucks, payment/visit/reminder history, notes, favorite payment method, average stay, custom pricing, risk score and loyalty score.

nodes.label: Payment History (Immutable)
nodes.rationale: Every payment is stored with receipt, method, employee, amount, notes and date, and is never deleted — append-only because payment disputes and staff accountability both depend on the record being unrewritable.

nodes.label: Audit Log
nodes.rationale: Tracks created, edited, renewed, cancelled, refund attempt, reminder sent and search performed. Logging refund attempts and searches (not just mutations) is what makes the no-refund rule and the reminder cadence auditable after the fact.

nodes.label: Color Coded Notifications
nodes.rationale: Green paid, orange expiring, red expired, blue monthly customer, purple frequent visitor — status is legible at a glance in daylight without reading text.

nodes.label: Search Everywhere (CTRL + K)
nodes.rationale: A single command palette over truck, trailer, company, phone, license and payment so no entity requires knowing which page it lives on.

nodes.label: Future Features Roadmap
nodes.rationale: QR passes, SMS payments, online booking, LPR, OCR of paper passes, camera detection, gate integration, customer portal, mobile app, driver wallet, fuel integration, loyalty, revenue prediction, occupancy heatmaps — parked deliberately so they do not compete with the core manual-work removal.

nodes.label: UX Rules (3-Click Maximum)
nodes.rationale: Maximum three clicks to any action, nothing cluttered, everything searchable, keyboard shortcuts everywhere, and mobile/tablet/desktop all first-class because the owner works from the lot on a phone.

nodes.label: Coding Standards
nodes.rationale: Small reusable components, strong typing, clean architecture, no duplicate logic, no hardcoded values, environment variables only, feature flags, unit tests, logging and graceful error handling.
nodes.community_name: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything

nodes.label: AI Development Rules (Plan, Build, Verify, Optimize)
nodes.rationale: Plan before code, then build, verify, optimize; never over-engineer; prefer simplicity, maintainability and speed. The ordering exists to stop speculative abstraction before it is justified by a verified behavior.
nodes.norm_label: ai development rules (plan, build, verify, optimize)
nodes.community_name: Core Principle: The Software Remembers Everything

nodes.label: Success Metric
nodes.rationale: Success is defined behaviorally, not by shipped features: no paper passes, no manual monthly board checks, no remembered renewal dates, any truck identified in under one second, automatic reminders, daily-to-monthly conversion, unprompted insights, hours saved every week.
